overview: White opens with a knight to the rim, aiming for c4 or b5 and keeping the pawns flexible. It is an irregular opening chosen to leave known theory; the knight on a3 is a little misplaced, so White usually follows with c3 or c4, Nc4 and a normal development. Black can occupy the centre with ...e5 and ...d5 and is fine.

white_ideas.idea: Reroute the knight with Nc4 or Nb5 and then build with c4, g3 and Bg2.
Transpose to an English or a reversed set-up after e4 or c4.

black_ideas.idea: Take the centre with ...e5 and ...d5 and develop freely.
Punish the rim knight by gaining space and play ...c5 or ...d5 with tempo.

typical_structures.structure: Black pawn centre on e5 and d5 against White flank set-up with c4 and g3.

character.notes: Slow and flexible; nothing forces either side into tactics early.

gambit.notes: Just a knight move, no material is offered.

soundness.notes: Slightly inaccurate placement but sound; White loses no material and can fix the knight with Nc4.

structure.notes: Centre is undecided; White often reaches an English-type structure.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom open 1.Na3; it is chosen for surprise.

level.notes: A coach would not give it to a new player; it asks little memory but no clear plan either.

character.reason: Slow flexible opening neither forcing nor especially solid.

soundness.reason: The knight is awkward but not losing anything.

approach.reason: Seldom played by strong players, chosen for surprise.

level.reason: Not a beginner choice and no deep theory to learn.

plans.reason: No recognised plan from the table characterises it.
